intro: A lawyer from the city of ghats, Varanasi, who believes that a client's trust is the largest asset he will ever be asked to protect. Anand advises businesses, promoters, exporters, startups, investors and Non-Resident Indian families where significant capital and assets are at stake.
profile: Anand Kumar Maurya grew up in Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh, the city of ghats, where learning, patience and plain speaking are part of daily life. He carries those values into every mandate. He is the Founder and Principal Advocate of Maurya & Co., Advocates and Legal Consultants, with offices in Noida, New Delhi NCR and Varanasi, and his practice covers banking and finance, restructuring and insolvency, dispute resolution and arbitration, project and infrastructure, regulatory law under the RBI and SEBI frameworks, and cross-border disputes, alongside real estate, international trade and startup advisory.

His conviction is simple. A client should always know where he stands, what it will cost, and what outcome is realistic, before the first notice is sent. He gives that answer honestly, even when it is not the answer the client hoped for, and he stays personally accountable for the matter until it is closed. He believes the best lawyering often prevents a dispute rather than wins one, and that discretion is owed to every client, whatever the size of the matter.

That approach has earned him mandates of real scale. Most recently, he advised an Ahmedabad-based commercial property group on the complete financing structure for commercial properties in Ahmedabad and Goa valued at over ₹200 crore, from acquisition through to bank funding, covering structured finance, mezzanine capital and fund structuring. He currently represents a Non-Resident Indian client in a cross-border property dispute of approximately ₹15 crore, and in September 2026 he appeared as Independent Indian Law Expert before a Superior Court in the State of Georgia, USA. His wider work spans a ₹85 crore multi-lender infrastructure exposure, stressed portfolios of ₹100 crore to ₹130 crore, and matters involving State Bank of India, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, Standard Chartered and American Express.

Anand is also a writer and a teacher. He is a published author whose books are available on Amazon, and his columns on Indian banking regulation, insolvency and structured finance appear regularly in The Bar Bulletin. One of his research projects was honoured and launched by Shri M. Venkaiah Naidu, then Vice President of India. He lectures at universities, serves on an academic Board of Studies and judges international arbitration moots, because he believes a lawyer's duty includes passing on what he has learned. Teaching demands that he explain the law from first principles, and every client receives advice built on that same foundation.
motto: Clarity before cost. Honesty before comfort. Accountability until the matter is closed.

internationalEngagement.title: Independent Indian Law Expert, Superior Court, State of Georgia, USA
internationalEngagement.text: Appearing by video conference from New Delhi, Anand gave his opinion on Indian property law, title, transfer, documentation, transaction structure and regulatory compliance for assets situated in India, in a cross-border matter involving Indian property and commercial arrangements. When a dispute crosses jurisdictions, the law governing the underlying asset decides whether any order or settlement can actually be enforced. That is the advice he brings to foreign courts and counsel.
